title: Navigating the digital spectrum: Assessing political bias, stability, and downstream fairness in Large Language Models
measurement_description: The paper measures hate speech detection performance across different target identity groups, including specific religious groups (Muslims, Jews, Christians), to assess whether persona-conditioned political framing affects classification thresholds and performance.
findings: In the downstream hate speech detection task, detection performance varied systematically by target group. Averaged across the eight evaluated models, the highest detection capabilities among religious targets were for Christians (AUC 0.67), while Muslims had the lowest (AUC 0.59). Models also showed varying recall and precision across groups, such as Gemma 3 27B showing high recall (0.85) for Jewish targets. This variation is systematic rather than model-specific.
